content.body: I somehow only recently realized that the ES spec rightly uses real typographical (“curly”) quotation marks — rather than the ASCII character.
I wish all other specs would follow that example.

e.g. at https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/ecmascript-data-types-and-values.html#sec-ecmascript-language-types-string-type
> The String type is the set of all ordered sequences of zero or more 16-bit unsigned integer values (“elements”)

content.body: The only downside is that it makes typing spec text more annoying 😅
It’s a good learning experience for everybody 😀
Btw, you only noticed it now because we only did that change a few months ago! https://github.com/tc39/ecma262/pull/3861
aha!
bravo Richard Gibson
I noticed because I was looking at verbatim spec text copied from the spec into a C++ code comment.
And the copy/paste preserved the typographical quotes.
…which I think is also great — because in 2026 there’s no good reason for all of us to be avoiding the use of non-ASCII text in code comment

sideshowbarker: thoughts on https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/12951 ?
No strong opinion from the POV of conformance checking. But otherwise, last I understood, no implementors were interested (due to the perf issue).
Or wait, implementations already have to handle this, right?
So I guess the “performance issue” problem is, do we want to encourage author-developers to do something that’s gonna result in bad performance.
So then my opinion from the POV of conformance checking is: If it’s bad for performance, the we are right to continue disallowing it (for the HTML checker to report it).
